title: Estimating Vertical Ocean Velocity from Horizontal Currents: Linear and Depth-Conditional Neural-Network Approaches on a High-Resolution Regional Ocean Model
summary: A depth-conditioned CNN estimates vertical ocean velocity from local horizontal currents in a high-resolution western-Mediterranean simulation, with two independent out-of-sample regions. Results show a depth- and domain-limited nonlinear advantage at the deepest transition-region levels; the evidence is simulation-based, one winter snapshot, and not observational ocean validation.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Results §§3.2–3.4 quantify depth-decaying vertical-velocity correlation and show the FiLM model’s limited deep-level advantage on the transition region, not uniformly across domains.
evidence.unknown: Two out-of-sample geographic domains and 274 random-seed realizations evaluate transfer and numerical uncertainty; the source states sensitivity to input noise and seasonal limits.
evidence.ai_role: Methods §§2.4–2.5 use local horizontal-velocity stencils with a per-level linear baseline and a depth-conditioned FiLM CNN to estimate vertical velocity.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
